summary.name: Point
summary.one_liner: Point is an open-source macOS push-to-talk dictation app that lets you circle part of the screen while speaking and sends your words plus a marked-up screenshot to Claude Code, Cursor, or any chat.
use_cases: Dictating text into any Mac app by holding a key
Sending a spoken request plus a screenshot of a circled screen area to an AI coding agent
Giving voice instructions to Claude Code or Cursor about on-screen content
Keeping voice data private with on-device transcription
Searching past voice captures and transcripts
summary.what_it_does:
Point is a push-to-talk app: holding the Option key records speech, and releasing it inserts the transcript at the cursor in any app. Press and drag to circle part of the screen while talking, and on release the app sends the transcript and a screenshot of the circled area to an agent such as Claude Code, Cursor, or any chat. Double-tapping Option opens a sticky notes pad that saves as you type. A searchable history stores each capture with its screenshot, transcript, and recording. Speech is transcribed with Apple's on-device speech engine, and the page says no account or server is used.</what_it_does>
<parameter name="pricing">open source
notable: Circle part of the screen while speaking to send a marked-up screenshot with your words
Transcription runs on-device via Apple's speech engine; no audio uploaded
Roughly 1,800 lines of Swift, readable before running
Alternative trigger keys: Right Option, Left Control, Right Command, or Fn
caveats: Not yet notarized by Apple, so macOS may block the DMG and require Open Anyway in Privacy & Security
Needs Accessibility, Microphone, and Screen Recording permissions
